bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet described as 'Asset light Debt-Free balance sheet with cash reserves of more than ₹800Cr.'; Q1FY27 highlights repeat Cash* > ₹800 crore and Zero debt, where the asterisk defines cash as 'Cash & Cash Equivalents including marketable securities'.
- Liquidity is explicitly earmarked as an acquisition war-chest for strategic inorganic opportunities in India and globally, and for expanding sovereign cloud via partnership.
- MD & CEO frames the priorities as 'backed by disciplined capital allocation and strong governance' to create long-term value; the company is described as 'Professionally Managed, led by an experienced Board and Management'.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Entrenched incumbency in nation-critical registries: custodian of India's tax and pension databases, operating the Tax Information Network for the Income Tax Department and serving as the first and largest CRA for NPS and APY with over 16 years of operation.
- Dominant, regulator-conferred market share - 97% cumulative share in CRA services (NPS/APY/UPS) and approximately 64% cumulative market share in Tax Services.
- Phygital distribution moat - over 5 lakh active TIN and PAN centres, 1,00,000+ Point of Presence centres, 400+ banking partners and reach across 12,000+ pin codes in 28 states and 8 UTs, giving deep last-mile reach into Tier II and Tier III markets.
- High switching costs and regulatory licensing barriers: UIDAI, CCA, RBI, PFRDA and Income Tax Department authorisations plus certifications (MeitY, PCI-DSS, SOC 1/2/3, ISO, HIPAA) that are prerequisites for regulated deployments.
- Recurring, annuity-like revenue base - transaction-based and annuity income from core businesses complemented by long-term implementation and managed-services revenue from large DPI projects, providing resilience and revenue visibility.
- Asset-light, debt-free balance sheet with cash and marketable securities of over Rs 850 crore, giving capacity to invest without leverage.
- Indigenous technology differentiation in cloud and infosec - a Made-in-India Quantum-Safe Data Vault, an open-source architecture that lowers total cost of ownership, and patented green technologies for energy efficiency.
- Engineering depth: 400+ technology professionals, specialised Centres of Excellence and cloud-native modular architecture proven at population scale, built to support millions of events per second.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and mandate dependence — MD&A Threats note that regulatory change could impact the scope, pricing, timelines and continuity of existing mandates and create opportunities for new competitors. Protean's core revenue rests on mandates conferred by government bodies and regulators (Income Tax Department, UIDAI, PFRDA, CERSAI, IRDAI), so terms are set by the counterparty rather than the market.
- Evolution of the PAN ecosystem, including PAN 2.0 — Management flags that ongoing evolution of the PAN ecosystem, including the implementation and transition associated with PAN 2.0, could influence the structure of PAN-related services and the Company's role across the value chain. Tax services accounted for 50% of turnover in FY26 per the BRSR products table, so any repositioning is structurally material.
- Cybersecurity and data protection — Operating critical digital infrastructure and processing sensitive citizen data at scale exposes the Company to evolving cybersecurity, privacy and data protection risks, with increasing regulatory and compliance requirements. The BRSR material-issues table classifies 'Data security & privacy' as a Risk with negative financial implications, noting a breach could cause loss of reputation, decline in customer confidence and legal and regulatory fines.
- Rapid technological evolution and obsolescence — Accelerating advances in AI, cloud, cybersecurity and other emerging technologies require continuous investment and capability enhancement, while rapid technology cycles may increase the risk of obsolescence.
- Execution and technology resilience on mission-critical platforms — Increasing scale and complexity of mission-critical digital platforms heighten the importance of operational resilience, cybersecurity preparedness and uninterrupted service delivery; any disruption could affect stakeholder confidence and business continuity.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — The BRSR reports IT enabled services as 100% of turnover, and the segment note states the Group is mainly engaged in providing IT services conducted in only one geographic segment, viz India, so Ind AS 108 segment disclosure is not applicable. Exports are only 0.83% of turnover, leaving revenue concentrated in a single activity and a single geography.
- Customer-grievance volume at scale — The BRSR complaints table records 1,85,875 customer complaints filed during FY2025-26 with 1,521 pending at year end (against 3,83,949 filed and 3,80,376 pending in FY2024-25), a structural service-quality exposure inherent in operating citizen-facing platforms at population scale.
- Employee attrition and talent dependence — The BRSR turnover-rate table shows the permanent-employee attrition rate rose to 13.3% in FY2025-26 from 11.1% in FY2024-25. With 839 permanent employees and 400+ technology professionals, and management identifying talent management and development as a material issue, continued delivery on large RFP-led mandates depends on retaining specialist engineering capability.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as 'Pioneer and Architect of India's DPI journey; custodian of nation-critical databases like Tax and Pension records', with over 3 decades of experience and 21+ nationally critical e-Governance stacks enabled across several ministries.
- Claims market leadership in Taxation (cumulative 64% share) and Central Recordkeeping Agency (97% market share), plus a 'Dominant player in Digital Identity Services'.
- States it is the 'Sole entity providing all four foundational identity services' — eSign, eKYC, Online PAN Verification, and Aadhaar Issuance & Authentication — positioning it as preferred partner to BFSI atop foundational digital identity rails.
- Strategy framed as three pillars: Build & Operate Digital Public Infrastructure, Enabling Enterprise Digital Ecosystems, and Global Expansion (Taking India Stack Global), aligned to the Government's strategy of taking India Stack global.
- Revenue model described as 'Annuity & Transactional revenue with predictable stability'; within CRA the deck splits the dual revenue stream as Transactional (8%) and annuity (92%).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Regulation] Revised PAN documentation norms effective 1 April 2026 temporarily impacted industry-wide PAN issuances during April and May; the deck states volumes normalised from June onwards, and that Protean's share rose from 59% in FY26 to 62% in Q1FY27 (described as 'nearly 275 bps increase').
- [Leadership] This is the MD & CEO's stated 'first quarterly update' in the role.
- [Pass-through] Identity Services revenue for FY22 carries the note '*adjusted for revision in UIDAI Charges from Rs.20 per transaction to ~ ₹ 3 per transaction which is pass through cost for the company'.
- [Reporting basis] The deck cautions that 'ID Services transaction volumes include internal services while revenue reflects only external billing'.
- [Regulatory tailwind cited] NPS employer contribution increased from 10% to 14% under the new tax regime, and PFRDA has eased investment & withdrawal norms with exit age raised to 85 years.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Protean designs, implements and operates nationally critical digital platforms for governments, regulators, enterprises and financial institutions. Its established businesses are Tax Services (PAN/TAN issuance, e-TDS return processing, Online PAN Verification and the Tax Information Network run on behalf of the Income Tax Department) and Central Recordkeeping Agency services for the National Pension System, Atal Pension Yojana and the Unified Pension Scheme. Around these it runs Identity Services (Aadhaar authentication, e-KYC, licensed eSign), Open Digital Ecosystems, a MeitY-certified cloud and information-security business, and a Data Stack of API and consent-based data-exchange platforms, delivered through a nationwide assisted-service network.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Tax Services:** Tax Information Network (TIN), PAN issuance, TAN issuance, e-TDS return processing, Online PAN Verification (OPV), Form 24G / AIN services
- **CRA Services:** NPS Central Recordkeeping Agency, Atal Pension Yojana (APY), Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), eNPS, NPS Vatsalya, D-Remit, Pension Sarathi, NPS Pension Planner
- **Identity Services:** Aadhaar Authentication (ASA/AUA), e-KYC (KSA/KUA), Licensed eSign services, Online PAN Verification, Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK)
- **Open Digital Ecosystems:** ONDC (founding technology partner), BECKN Gateway and Registry for the Kochi Open Mobility Network, Bima Sugam, Central AgriStack, Open AgriNet, Vidyasaarathi, ONEST, ABDM CMIS / PHR for Aapla Dawakhana clinics
- **Cloud and InfoSec:** Protean On-Premises Cloud, Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Storage as a Service (StaaS), Desktop as a Service (DaaS) and Virtual Office, Managed Security Operations Centre (SOC), Analytics as a Service, AI in a Box / Sovereign AI Cloud-in-a-Box, API Life Cycle Management Solution
- **Data Stack:** RISE with Protean (API marketplace), AI-enabled CKYC, eSignPro, Account Aggregator, Quantum-Safe Data Vault, Secure API Gateway
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Protean Infosec Services Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding per BRSR Section A item 23 and Form AOC-1; information-security services business (VAPT/WAPT, GRC, Managed SOC, DPDPA assessment and consent management); participates in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives
- Protean Account Aggregator Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding; formerly NSDL e-Governance Account Aggregator Limited; RBI-licensed consent-based financial data sharing platform; participates in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives
- Protean International DMCC — subsidiary: Wholly-owned UAE subsidiary, 100% shareholding, incorporated 27 August 2024, set up to lead international IT/ITeS projects; reporting currency AED; does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives
- Protean eGov Technologies Australia Pty Ltd — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding (shown as Protean e-Gov Australia Pty Ltd in BRSR Section A item 23); formerly NSDL e-Governance Australia Pty Ltd; does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives
- NSDL e-Governance (Malaysia) SDN BHD — subsidiary: Former subsidiary, liquidated on 16 December 2024, named in the related-party note

- NSE Investments Limited (erstwhile NSE Strategic Investments Corporation Limited) — related party: Listed in the related-party note under 'Entities having substantial interest', till 25 November 2024
- NSDL Payments Bank — related party: 4.95% strategic stake acquired during FY2025-26; partnership to co-develop certified digital banking technologies for the BFSI sector

outlook.body: Scaling certified banking tech stack to other payment banks/NBFCs; monetizing AI-driven credit surrogate models; expanding into AgriStack/education loan verticals via shared infrastructure
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Diversify beyond the two legacy engines (Tax Services and CRA) by scaling New Businesses - CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0, Bima Sugam, Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Data Stack, cloud services and international DPI - which lifted their share of operating revenue from 4% in FY2024-25 to 10% in FY2025-26.
- Maintain a balanced revenue mix of transaction-based, annuity and project-led income, so that stable recurring revenue from core businesses is complemented by long-term implementation and managed-services revenue from large DPI projects.
- Allocate capital prudently towards technology modernisation, digital platform development, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and execution capabilities, while preserving a debt-free balance sheet and financial flexibility.
- Expand into the BFSI ecosystem through the 4.95% strategic stake in NSDL Payments Bank, co-developing certified digital banking technologies on the back of Protean's DPI expertise.
- Take India Stack global - export proven DPI capabilities to governments across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa, prioritising scalable and interoperable public platforms.
- Build a sovereign cloud and information-security franchise on the open-source, MeitY-certified platform, differentiated by data sovereignty, indigenous quantum-safe technology, lower total cost of ownership and patented green energy-efficiency technologies.
- Deepen the Data Stack (RISE with Protean, AI-enabled CKYC, eSignPro, Account Aggregator) to create scalable and recurring revenue that complements and strengthens the core identity solutions business.
- Evolve the agriculture business from project-based implementation into a broader platform ecosystem spanning infrastructure, data exchanges, marketplaces, credit enablement and AI-based advisory services.
- Extend pension reach by identifying and activating new channels and channel partners to increase NPS penetration at scale, supported by Subscriber Awareness Programmes and continued CRA technology modernisation (API suites, UI/UX redesign, a single mobile application).
- Invest in Gen AI, machine learning and blockchain - natural-language search for ONDC, AI-assisted identity verification, biometric authentication and a blockchain-based verifiable-credentials platform under development.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Protean is an asset-light services business, so its expansion is footprint, platform build-out and mandate wins rather than plant capex. The largest FY2025-26 win is a Rs 1,370 crore UIDAI mandate for district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendras with an initial contract period of six years; 102 Aadhaar Seva Kendras were operational as of July 2026 across 25 states and Union Territories, with a state-wise rollout spanning 37 states/UTs. Other mandates adding footprint are the Rs 100 crore Bima Sugam India Federation mandate for a unified digital insurance marketplace, a Rs 25 crore AI-powered digital agriculture platform for Ethiopia, and CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0 (an INR 161 crore mandate secured in FY2025 to build the upgraded Central KYC Records Registry, on which Protean acts as System Integrator and now moves from implementation to steady-state operations). Physical and platform infrastructure comprises 2 disaster-resilient Tier-III data centres, over 5 lakh active TIN and PAN centres, 1,00,000+ Point of Presence centres and reach across 12,000+ pin codes in 28 states and 8 UTs; the AR notes no new PAN Centre was registered in FY2025-26. On the platform side the Company launched three new solutions during the year - Sovereign AI Cloud-in-a-Box, the Quantum-Safe Secure Data Vault and e-NPS Express Onboarding - and expanded the RISE with Protean API marketplace with Mobile and Image Enrichment, Unified Vehicle RC, DigiLocker 3.0, Offline Aadhaar Verification, Video KYC and AI-driven verification. Capital was directed to technology modernisation, digital platform enhancement, product development, cybersecurity and AI, plus a Rs 30.2 crore strategic investment for a 4.95% stake in NSDL Payments Bank. International build-out runs through Protean International DMCC (100% UAE subsidiary, incorporated 27 August 2024) leading international IT/ITeS projects, the Open AgriNet setup with hi.ai in Ethiopia, a first-of-its-kind DPI-in-a-Box for education in Morocco, and presence across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. The MeitY-certified open-source sovereign cloud platform is being scaled for large-scale e-governance and enterprise workloads, and Protean InfoSec has applied for CERT-In certification to address the VAPT/WAPT market.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's growth composition remains services-led and formalisation-driven, which management says expands the addressable base for identity, tax, pension and data-exchange infrastructure.
- The fiscal stance combines consolidation with sustained capital expenditure, favouring platform-based delivery models that lower the unit cost of public service provision.
- Policy architecture is shifting from building digital rails to monetising and exporting them, evident in the tax treatment of data centres and AI-linked research funding.
- For providers of population-scale digital infrastructure the consequential shift is compositional rather than cyclical: growth differentials between economies are increasingly explained by the depth of digital and technology infrastructure, reframing DPI from a governance efficiency measure into a determinant of national competitiveness.
- Tax Services growth was supported by higher PAN issuance volumes ahead of the regulatory changes in PAN documentation norms effective from April 2026, plus market share gains through the extensive service network.
- CRA growth is driven by PFRDA regulatory initiatives simplifying onboarding, augmenting investment and withdrawal flexibility and democratising access through offerings such as NPS Swasthya and NPS Sanchay, plus healthy subscriber additions and increased corporate participation.
- Identity Services continues to benefit from the expanding DPI ecosystem and increasing digital adoption, with growing take-up of value-added offerings including eSignPro and RISE with Protean.
- Cloud growth drivers cited: accelerated digital adoption across finance, healthcare, manufacturing and government; national programmes such as Digital India, e-governance and data localisation mandates; growth of AI, analytics, edge computing and pay-as-you-go models; and increased cloud investment by public and private sector entities.
- Data Stack demand drivers cited: AI adoption in public services requiring real-time processing and ML pipelines; cloud-native and edge adoption driving modular containerised components; unified-platform programmes such as Digital India and Gati Shakti; and rising focus on data localisation and citizen data protection.
- New regulation is a major driver of cybersecurity adoption - the DPDP Act 2023 and draft 2025 DPDP rules are expected to drive a significant surge in corporate spending on privacy and compliance services over the next three years, with Protean InfoSec already growing more than 75% year-on-year.
- Union Budget 2026-27 provisions bearing on the digital economy: MeitY allocated Rs 21,633 crore, the IndiaAI Mission Rs 1,000 crore within a multi-year outlay of Rs 10,372 crore, and a Research, Development and Innovation Fund with a Rs 1 lakh crore corpus.
- Management notes investments made during the year in talent, technology and execution capabilities to support large RFP-led mandates are expected to support future revenue growth as projects mature and scale.
- Order book exceeded Rs 1,500 crore as on March 31, 2026, providing strong medium-term revenue visibility.
- Key wins during the year included Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Bima Sugam and the Ethiopia Digital Agriculture Platform.
- The Company secured strategic mandates across digital identity, insurance, financial services and agriculture, including CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0, Bima Sugam, Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Data Stack, cloud services and international DPI opportunities.

currentContext.expansion: Protean is an asset-light services business, so its expansion is footprint, platform build-out and mandate wins rather than plant capex. The largest FY2025-26 win is a Rs 1,370 crore UIDAI mandate for district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendras with an initial contract period of six years; 102 Aadhaar Seva Kendras were operational as of July 2026 across 25 states and Union Territories, with a state-wise rollout spanning 37 states/UTs. Other mandates adding footprint are the Rs 100 crore Bima Sugam India Federation mandate for a unified digital insurance marketplace, a Rs 25 crore AI-powered digital agriculture platform for Ethiopia, and CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0 (an INR 161 crore mandate secured in FY2025 to build the upgraded Central KYC Records Registry, on which Protean acts as System Integrator and now moves from implementation to steady-state operations). Physical and platform infrastructure comprises 2 disaster-resilient Tier-III data centres, over 5 lakh active TIN and PAN centres, 1,00,000+ Point of Presence centres and reach across 12,000+ pin codes in 28 states and 8 UTs; the AR notes no new PAN Centre was registered in FY2025-26. Capital was directed to technology modernisation, digital platform enhancement, product development, cybersecurity and AI, plus a Rs 30.2 crore strategic investment for a 4.95% stake in NSDL Payments Bank. International build-out runs through Protean International DMCC (100% UAE subsidiary, incorporated 27 August 2024) leading international IT/ITeS projects, the Open AgriNet setup with hi.ai in Ethiopia, a first-of-its-kind DPI-in-a-Box for education in Morocco, and presence across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. The MeitY-certified open-source sovereign cloud platform is being scaled for large-scale e-governance and enterprise workloads, and Protean InfoSec has applied for CERT-In certification to address the VAPT/WAPT market.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's growth composition remains services-led and formalisation-driven, which management says expands the addressable base for identity, tax, pension and data-exchange infrastructure.
- The fiscal stance combines consolidation with sustained capital expenditure, favouring platform-based delivery models that lower the unit cost of public service provision.
- Policy architecture is shifting from building digital rails to monetising and exporting them, evident in the tax treatment of data centres and AI-linked research funding.
- For providers of population-scale digital infrastructure the consequential shift is compositional rather than cyclical: growth differentials between economies are increasingly explained by the depth of digital and technology infrastructure, reframing DPI from a governance efficiency measure into a determinant of national competitiveness.
- Tax Services growth was supported by higher PAN issuance volumes ahead of the regulatory changes in PAN documentation norms effective from April 2026, plus market share gains through the extensive service network.
- CRA growth is driven by PFRDA regulatory initiatives simplifying onboarding, augmenting investment and withdrawal flexibility and democratising access through offerings such as NPS Swasthya and NPS Sanchay, plus healthy subscriber additions and increased corporate participation.
- Identity Services continues to benefit from the expanding DPI ecosystem and increasing digital adoption, with growing take-up of value-added offerings including eSignPro and RISE with Protean.
- Cloud growth drivers cited: accelerated digital adoption across finance, healthcare, manufacturing and government; national programmes such as Digital India, e-governance and data localisation mandates; growth of AI, analytics, edge computing and pay-as-you-go models; and increased cloud investment by public and private sector entities.
- Data Stack demand drivers cited: AI adoption in public services requiring real-time processing and ML pipelines; cloud-native and edge adoption driving modular containerised components; unified-platform programmes such as Digital India and Gati Shakti; and rising focus on data localisation and citizen data protection.
- New regulation is a major driver of cybersecurity adoption - the DPDP Act 2023 and draft 2025 DPDP rules are expected to drive a significant surge in corporate spending on privacy and compliance services over the next three years, with Protean InfoSec already growing more than 75% year-on-year.
- Union Budget 2026-27 provisions bearing on the digital economy: MeitY allocated Rs 21,633 crore, the IndiaAI Mission Rs 1,000 crore within a multi-year outlay of Rs 10,372 crore, and a Research, Development and Innovation Fund with a Rs 1 lakh crore corpus.
- Management notes investments made during the year in talent, technology and execution capabilities to support large RFP-led mandates are expected to support future revenue growth as projects mature and scale.
- Order book exceeded Rs 1,500 crore as on March 31, 2026, providing strong medium-term revenue visibility.
- Key wins during the year included Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Bima Sugam and the Ethiopia Digital Agriculture Platform.
- The Company secured strategic mandates across digital identity, insurance, financial services and agriculture, including CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0, Bima Sugam, Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Data Stack, cloud services and international DPI opportunities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Protean is an asset-light services business, so its expansion is footprint, platform build-out and mandate wins rather than plant capex. The largest FY2025-26 win is a Rs 1,370 crore UIDAI mandate for district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendras with an initial contract period of six years; 102 Aadhaar Seva Kendras were operational as of July 2026 across 25 states and Union Territories, with a state-wise rollout spanning 37 states/UTs. Other mandates adding footprint are the Rs 100 crore Bima Sugam India Federation mandate for a unified digital insurance marketplace, a Rs 25 crore AI-powered digital agriculture platform for Ethiopia, and CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0 (an INR 161 crore mandate secured in FY2025 to build the upgraded Central KYC Records Registry, on which Protean acts as System Integrator and now moves from implementation to steady-state operations). Physical and platform infrastructure comprises 2 disaster-resilient Tier-III data centres, over 5 lakh active TIN and PAN centres, 1,00,000+ Point of Presence centres and reach across 12,000+ pin codes in 28 states and 8 UTs; the AR notes no new PAN Centre was registered in FY2025-26. On the platform side the Company launched three new solutions during the year - Sovereign AI Cloud-in-a-Box, the Quantum-Safe Secure Data Vault and e-NPS Express Onboarding - and expanded the RISE with Protean API marketplace with Mobile and Image Enrichment, Unified Vehicle RC, DigiLocker 3.0, Offline Aadhaar Verification, Video KYC and AI-driven verification. Capital was directed to technology modernisation, digital platform enhancement, product development, cybersecurity and AI, plus a Rs 30.2 crore strategic investment for a 4.95% stake in NSDL Payments Bank. International build-out runs through Protean International DMCC (100% UAE subsidiary, incorporated 27 August 2024) leading international IT/ITeS projects, the Open AgriNet setup with hi.ai in Ethiopia, a first-of-its-kind DPI-in-a-Box for education in Morocco, and presence across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. The MeitY-certified open-source sovereign cloud platform is being scaled for large-scale e-governance and enterprise workloads, and Protean InfoSec has applied for CERT-In certification to address the VAPT/WAPT market.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: highly confident, strategic, and long-term oriented; emphasized co-creation, not transactional partnership; framed as ‘perfect marriage’ of DPI and financial inclusion mandate

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Entrenched incumbency in nation-critical registries: custodian of India's tax and pension databases, operating the Tax Information Network for the Income Tax Department and serving as the first and largest CRA for NPS and APY with over 16 years of operation.
- Dominant, regulator-conferred market share - 97% cumulative share in CRA services (NPS/APY/UPS) and approximately 64% cumulative market share in Tax Services.
- Phygital distribution moat - over 5 lakh active TIN and PAN centres, 1,00,000+ Point of Presence centres, 400+ banking partners and reach across 12,000+ pin codes in 28 states and 8 UTs, giving deep last-mile reach into Tier II and Tier III markets.
- High switching costs and regulatory licensing barriers: UIDAI, CCA, RBI, PFRDA and Income Tax Department authorisations plus certifications (MeitY, PCI-DSS, SOC 1/2/3, ISO, HIPAA) that are prerequisites for regulated deployments.
- Recurring, annuity-like revenue base - transaction-based and annuity income from core businesses complemented by long-term implementation and managed-services revenue from large DPI projects, providing resilience and revenue visibility.
- Asset-light, debt-free balance sheet with cash and marketable securities of over Rs 850 crore, giving capacity to invest without leverage.
- Indigenous technology differentiation in cloud and infosec - a Made-in-India Quantum-Safe Data Vault, an open-source architecture that lowers total cost of ownership, and patented green technologies for energy efficiency.
- Engineering depth: 400+ technology professionals, specialised Centres of Excellence and cloud-native modular architecture proven at population scale, built to support millions of events per second.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: regulatory scrutiny on cross-investment in payment banks; potential perception of reduced independence when pitching to competitors; slower-than-expected adoption of co-created solutions

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 3M active customers at NSDL Payments Bank (as of Sep 2025) provide Protean with a real-world, regulated sandbox to validate and certify its AI-driven fintech products—this is a rare, high-fidelity testing ground unavailable to pure-play SaaS vendors

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify beyond the two legacy engines (Tax Services and CRA) by scaling New Businesses - CERSAI CKYCRR 2.0, Bima Sugam, Aadhaar Seva Kendras, Data Stack, cloud services and international DPI - which lifted their share of operating revenue from 4% in FY2024-25 to 10% in FY2025-26.
- Maintain a balanced revenue mix of transaction-based, annuity and project-led income, so that stable recurring revenue from core businesses is complemented by long-term implementation and managed-services revenue from large DPI projects.
- Allocate capital prudently towards technology modernisation, digital platform …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation] Revised PAN documentation norms effective 1 April 2026 temporarily impacted industry-wide PAN issuances during April and May; the deck states volumes normalised from June onwards, and that Protean's share rose from 59% in FY26 to 62% in Q1FY27 (described as 'nearly 275 bps increase').
- [Leadership] This is the MD & CEO's stated 'first quarterly update' in the role.
- [Pass-through] Identity Services revenue for FY22 carries the note '*adjusted for revision in UIDAI Charges from Rs.20 per transaction to ~ ₹ 3 per transaction which is pass through cost for the company'.
- [Reporting basis] The deck cautions that 'ID Services transaction volumes include internal services while revenue reflects only external billing'.
- [Regulatory tailwind cited] NPS employer contribution increased from 10% to 14% under the new tax regime, and PFRDA has eased investment & withdrawal norms with exit age raised to 85 years.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
